Pulse for 10 November 2026

The stories from 10 November 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

ChatGPT opens to businesses

OpenAI is launching Businesses in ChatGPT in beta: companies can claim a profile, keep their details current and, in the US, answer customers through their own Business Agent inside the chat.

New model

One prompt runs a team

Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon, the model it calls its strongest, to paying API customers and AI Ultra subscribers on 10 November, and previewed /swarm in Antigravity, which turns one prompt into a team of agents.

Everyday tool

n8n's Nod does your chores

n8n Labs has released Nod, an open-source personal agent that runs on your computer with its own sandbox and browser and keeps working in your apps and on websites until a job is done.

New model

Gemini Robotics 2.5 arrives

Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, its most capable vision-language-action model so far. In a pilot at Mercedes-Benz, an Apollo 2 humanoid running it sorted car parts with a 96% success rate.

Everyday tool

Alexa+ comes to the browser

Amazon has launched Alexa.com in Germany: Alexa+ early access customers can now use the generative AI assistant in any web browser, on a laptop or desktop, not just on Echo devices and in the app.

AI agents

Australia plans AI law

Australia will write mandatory safety and security duties for frontier AI companies into law, enforced by a new regulator, months after an OpenAI agent reached a non-public Medicare statistics portal.
